profile.campus: Data4 MIL01 campus, Cornaredo, Milan (217 MW / 20 ha campus total, distinct from the separate MIL02 site in Vittuone)

source.basis: Operator campus page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This building, tagged DC01, is one of eight mapped structures on Data4 Italia MIL01 campus at Via Monzoro 101-105 in Cornaredo, a suburb of Milan, Italy. Data4, styled DATA4, is a European data center developer and operator founded in 2006 and headquartered in Paris, France, which its own 2019 published materials describe as controlled by AXA, the French insurance and asset-management group, though the specific AXA entity and any co-investors could not be independently confirmed this session. Data4 own site describes a six-country European footprint spanning France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany, and Greece, totaling roughly ten campuses, 1.5 gigawatts of capacity, and 165,000 square meters of IT space group-wide. Data4 has operated in Italy since 2012, developing the Cornaredo campus in progressive phases according to the company own Italian-language press materials. As of an October 2018 company announcement, three data centers were fully operational on the campus with nearly all of that space allocated to customers, and Data4 had banked land for up to seven additional buildings while planning a fourth-generation facility of roughly 2,000 square meters and 3 megawatts of IT power to a Tier 4 design target. That fourth building was formally inaugurated at a June 2019 campus event. Data4 current Milan-area location page describes the Cornaredo site, referred to as MIL01, as a 217 megawatt, 20 hectare campus, distinct from a separate second Milan-area site in Vittuone known as MIL02. No Data4 source reviewed breaks the 217 megawatt campus figure down by individual building, and no source explained what distinguishes the DC numbering from the DCL numbering seen on other buildings in this cluster, so no capacity or square footage figure specific to DC01 alone is asserted here, and no tenant is named.
profile.capacity_note: Campus level total published, 170 MW and 20 hectares, not broken down per building, so no per building MW or square footage figure is recorded.
profile.research_note: Campus-level 217 MW / 20 ha figure from Data4 own Milan location page, explicitly not assigned to this individual building. Build-out history (3 operational 2018, 4th inaugurated June 2019, land banked for up to 7 more) from Data4 own Italian press materials. DC vs DCL naming distinction not explained by any Data4 source, flagged as unconfirmed OSM-side convention.

reading.body:
Data4's MIL01 campus near Milan has 170 MW of electrical capacity across 20 hectares, but this power is distributed among at least eight separate buildings with no per-building breakdown published.

The campus structure reflects how large data center operators consolidate infrastructure. A single address, unified power supply, and contiguous land parcel create operational efficiency. The lack of per-building power figures is common when operators design campuses as integrated units rather than discrete facilities, which simplifies grid interconnection and cooling distribution.

For AI workloads, what matters is the 170 MW total available to the campus. This is the constraint on how much compute can run here. The data does not reveal how much of this capacity is in use, reserved, or available for new tenants, nor does it distinguish between buildings optimized for different workload types.

The Milan location provides no information about power sources, grid characteristics, or the regional Italian grid's ability to support additional AI infrastructure. That context determines whether this 170 MW represents genuine headroom for AI scaling or is already committed to other uses.
